clue.text: Plucky player has time to take in a measure of inflation

indicators.note: the word has opens up to take in the inflation measure, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
RPI is the Retail Price Index, the British measure of inflation

explanation.surface: A brave musician gets time off to look into the latest inflation figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' looks like a word for brave, but here it means plucking strings. The Retail Price Index (RPI) is a British inflation measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpist plucks strings, so a punning 'plucky player' is someone playing the harp.

clue.text: A couple regularly query lay

parts.note: to couple is to pair or mate, so the verb mate fits

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from query keeps its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Two people keep asking questions of someone outside the profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' is the adjective meaning non-professional, as in a lay preacher, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay person lacks professional training, which is exactly what an amateur is.

clue.text: Spiritual number brings in a grand, perhaps

indicators.note: the pious word and the number take the letter a into their middle, bringing it inside

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious, i.e. spiritual

explanation.surface: A gospel song earns its performer a thousand pounds, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiritual number' reads as a gospel song; it is two separate pieces. 'A grand' looks like £1,000 slang, but 'grand' is a kind of piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is one type of piano, so 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.

clue.text: On radio, avoids current lively pieces

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: to skirt something is to avoid it, giving skirts, and I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast steers clear of topical news items.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIRTS + I spoken together comes out close to the Italian plural scherzi. 'Current' reads as 'topical' in the surface, but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a playful, quick movement in music; the plural names several such lively pieces.

clue.text: Show £1 note in court

indicators.note: the pound-note slang word goes in between the letters of the court abbreviation

parts.note: ONCER is old British slang for a one-pound note

explanation.surface: A pound note is produced as evidence in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A ONCER was British slang for the old one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert is a musical performance put on for an audience, a kind of show.

clue.text: Spotted cat circle church group

parts.note: O is circle-shaped
CE is the Church of England
a lot is a set or group of items, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A leopard-spotted wild cat is seen circling a church group.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild American cat with a coat of dark spots and stripes.

clue.text: Highbrow Charlie Girl I visit briefly

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lass is a girl

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A sophisticated girl named Charlie says she will pop in for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter off CALL, giving CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical music and literature are seen as serious and intellectual, the taste of highbrows.

clue.text: Athlete swallows one more fluid

indicators.note: the athlete word takes the numeral inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a runner is an athlete
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A runner gulps down another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like a noun, a drink, but 'more fluid' is a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Runny means liquid or flowing, so runnier is the comparative for something flowing more freely.

clue.text: Ladies and gents engage a new supporter to defend a barman

indicators.note: the toilets take the following letters into their middle, as if hiring or engaging them

parts.note: JOHNS is American slang for toilets, which Ladies and Gents are

indicators.note: the supporting frame surrounds the letter a, guarding it

parts.note: a truss is a supporting frame or a surgical support

explanation.surface: Public toilets take on a new attendant to protect a man who works behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a bartender: it is someone who writes bars of music. The answer is the Austrian waltz composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music measured in bars, so the waltz king is cryptically a barman.

clue.text: Arthur's most perfect supporter had left party

indicators.note: left as a past verb means departed, so the word had goes away

parts.note: Sir Galahad was the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table

explanation.surface: King Arthur's finest knight walked out of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had left' reads as one verb phrase, but 'had' is the letters to remove and 'left' says they go.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or entertainment, a kind of party.

clue.text: Scream at English nurse: 'Listen to folk here!'

parts.note: a hoot is a cry, and also something hilarious, a scream
a nanny is a children's nurse

explanation.surface: Someone yells at an English nanny, telling her to pay attention to the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folk' reads as people, but means folk music.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal gathering where folk musicians play, a place for hearing folk songs.

clue.text: Popular place to wed Irish artist

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, is famous for quick weddings and divorces

explanation.surface: A painter from Ireland picks a fashionable wedding venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno in Nevada is known for its quick marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: A cricket club about to expel individual based on hearing

indicators.note: the club letters go about, around, the next pieces

parts.note: to oust is to expel
I, the single person, stands for an individual

explanation.surface: A cricket club is about to throw out a member on the strength of hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' wraps and 'to expel' is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic means relating to sound and the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Fish worker hauls in one diamond

indicators.note: the fish and worker together drag the numeral in between them, hauling it in

parts.note: brill is a European flatfish
a worker ant, the standard crossword worker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands a catch and finds a diamond in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish worker' reads as fisherman; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant is a diamond cut with many facets to maximise its sparkle.

clue.text: Attend new Hamlet, say, hosted by another mad royal

indicators.note: the king's name holds the other pieces within it, as a host holds guests

parts.note: King Lear goes mad; Hamlet, a prince, feigns madness, hence another
Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so an example of a Dane

explanation.surface: A new staging of Hamlet is put on by the company of another Shakespeare play about a mad king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet, say' is not the play but a Dane, the prince being Danish.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for listening attentively, i.e. paying attention.

clue.text: Aching to retain a hundred notes

indicators.note: the aching word keeps the numeral inside, retaining it

parts.note: sore means aching
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone in pain hangs on to a stack of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' reads as banknotes but means written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written musical notation of a piece, so it is a sheet of notes.

clue.text: Good eggs repelled cheat

indicators.note: driven back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice

explanation.surface: Decent people drove away a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good eggs' reads as 'decent people'; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick, a swindle that cheats its victim.

clue.text: Refrain from painting over articles in Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: painting is an example of art
LA is the French feminine for the, so two articles give LA twice

explanation.surface: Someone abstains from painting over articles in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb, to abstain, but it is the noun for a chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A tra-la-la is a nonsense chorus sung in a song, a refrain.

clue.text: A heavyweight boxer, extremely tidy, ignoring normal scales

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, the first and last, of tidy are used

explanation.surface: A heavyweight fighter, extremely neat, pays no attention to the weighing scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' looks like weighing scales but means musical scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written without a key, abandoning the usual major and minor scales.

clue.text: Top seed unwise to sacrifice length with racket

parts.note: the top seed in tennis is number one, written NO I

indicators.note: giving up one letter, as the word silly sacrifices the length abbreviation

parts.note: silly means unwise

explanation.surface: The leading tennis player foolishly gives up the length of shot, racket in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a tennis racket but means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud noise, so acting with racket means acting loudly.

clue.text: Piece played staccato with no introduction

indicators.note: the letters are played with, put into a new arrangement
the word loses its opening letter, its introduction

explanation.surface: A short-note passage is performed without any opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: STACCATO without its first letter gives TACCATO, which 'played' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, a musical piece.

clue.text: Home Counties guy across the Channel composed

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A man from south-east England heads over to France to write music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England. 'composed' suggests writing music; here it means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed means calm and collected, the same as serene.

clue.text: Greek goddess inspires a bar dance

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the goddess takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: Hera is queen of the Greek gods
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess motivates a dance in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bar dance' reads as one phrase; 'bar' is a verb synonym and 'dance' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance, famous from the aria in Carmen.

clue.text: Complete one part of play about books

indicators.note: the outer pieces go about, around, the books abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an act is a division of a play
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: One section of a drama is about books.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, stands for books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, i.e. complete.

clue.text: Bar last pair, voicing pique all at once

indicators.note: bar means except, so the final two letters are excluded

parts.note: tutting is voicing irritation by saying tut

explanation.surface: Except for the final pair of bars, the players express annoyance in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a musical bar but means except. 'voicing' is part of the synonym, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for the whole orchestra to play together, simultaneously.

clue.text: Pianist father and daughter were backing runner

parts.note: pa is father

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters of were are read in reverse

parts.note: a ski runs over snow, so it is a runner

explanation.surface: A father and daughter were supporting a racing runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as supporting, but it reverses WERE to EREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignacy Jan Paderewski was a celebrated Polish concert pianist, later prime minister.

clue.text: Lift to be arranged at end of dinner

indicators.note: only the final letter of dinner is used

explanation.surface: A ride home is to be organised once dinner is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' is not an anagram signal; TBA is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift that pulls skiers up the slope.

clue.text: Advocate getting shot of street obstacle

indicators.note: British slang for getting rid of, so the street abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a barrister is a courtroom advocate

explanation.surface: A lawyer gets rid of a road obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting shot of' is British slang for getting rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a fence or block that stands in the way, an obstacle.

clue.text: Musical theatre, at least initially

parts.note: the Lyric is a well-known theatre in London's West End

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of each of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A musical theatre production, at least to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is a London West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical means song-like and expressive, having a musical quality.
